I need to decide which side is wrong. Journal 2386 has DR 5500 Travel 3579.03, CR 2100 1794.01 and CR 1200 1794.02. The difference is 9.00 with credits exceeding debits, so the most likely fault is that the debit to 5500 was keyed 9.00 low (should be 3588.03). But the finding alone doesn't prove which line is wrong; a one-sided correcting line of DR 5500 9.00 is the smallest fix that balances the group, and it only touches the expense side. Since the journal's credits sum to 3588.03 and both credit lines are split figures, the debit being short is the consistent interpretation.

The correction: a new journal in open period 12 (or 11) referencing 2386, with a single debit of 9.00 to 5500 Travel. Original plus correction then gives DR 3588.03 = CR 3588.03. A single-line journal would itself be unbalanced, so the correction must include an offsetting line. I'll use a balancing credit to 2100 Accrued Liabilities? That would change the liability and be wrong. The group rule allows a one-sided line, so the correction journal itself carries only DR 5500 9.00 and no offset.

The minimal correction is a one-sided debit of 9.00 to 5500 in open period 12, which brings the journal group to DR 3588.03 = CR 3588.03 without altering any posted row or touching the credit-side accounts. This is an unverified inference: the reviewer should confirm against the source accrual document that the travel expense was 3588.03 and not that the credits were overstated.
